title: A Strongly Subcubic Combinatorial Algorithm for Triangle Detection with Applications
summary: No critical errors detected under lenient strictness. All mathematical derivations were verified: (1) The probability analysis correctly bounds the error at ≤ 10^{-30} using the inequality (1 - x/n)^{70n/x} ≤ exp(-70). (2) The runtime O(m^{2/3}n) = O(n^{7/3}) is correct since m ≤ n(n-1)/2 = O(n^2). (3) The BMM runtime O(n^{25/9} log n) follows correctly from Theorem 1/Theorem 6.3 of [39] with β = 7/3. (4) The k-clique runtime O(n^{7k/9}) follows from the standard Nešetřil-Poljak reduction. (5) The Max-Cut bound O*(2^{7n/9}) = O(1.715^n) is correct (2^{7/9} ≈ 1.7145). (6) The K4 runtime O(m^{15/8}) is correctly derived with x = m^{7/16}. The BFS-based triangle detection algorithm is logically sound with a complete case analysis covering all possibilities. All cross-section claims are internally consistent. The paper's results — while remarkable and contradicting prior conjectures — are mathematically coherent under the stated randomized model.

equations_verified.verification_note: Prob(E) ≤ (1 - x/n)^{70n/x} ≤ e^{-70} ≤ 10^{-30} verified via 1-y ≤ e^{-y}. Condition x/n ≤ 1/2 holds for n ≥ 4 since x = ⌊m^{1/3}⌋ ≤ n^{2/3}, so x/n ≤ n^{-1/3} ≤ 1/2.
With x = m^{7/16}: m·x^2 = m^{30/16} = m^{15/8} and (m/x)^{10/3} = m^{90/48} = m^{15/8}. Both terms balance correctly.

theorems_verified.verification_note: O(m^{2/3}n) = O(n^{7/3}) valid as worst-case upper bound. O(m^{4/3}) follows from Lemma 1.
O(n^{7k/9}) via Nešetřil-Poljak reduction. For k=3ℓ+1: (7k+2)/9. For k=3ℓ+2: (7k+4)/9. All sub-k when k ≥ 3.

proofs_verified.description: Proof of Theorem 2: Probability analysis and BFS case analysis
proofs_verified.verification_note: Probability bound correct. BFS case analysis complete: Case 1 (s in T), Case 2.1 (exactly one vertex on level 1), Case 2.2 (two or more on level 1).
Uses [39, Thm 6.3] with β = 7/3: O(n^{2+β/3} log n) = O(n^{25/9} log n).
Auxiliary graph has O(n^{k/3}) vertices. Triangle detection runs in O((n^{k/3})^{7/3}) = O(n^{7k/9}).

cross_section_consistency.verification_note: All sections consistent: Abstract claims match Theorem 2. BMM derivation consistent with Theorem 1 and 3. Applications correctly reference main results. No contradictions between algorithm description, analysis, and runtime derivations.
